channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Beyond Corner Patches: Semantics-Aware Backdoor Attack in Federated Learning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes SABLE, a semantics-aware backdoor attack for federated learning using in-distribution, visually plausible, semantically meaningful triggers.
  • Optimizes an aggregation-aware malicious objective with feature separation and parameter regularization to keep poisoned client updates close to benign ones.
  • Evaluates targeted attack success and benign accuracy on CelebA (hair-color) and GTSRB under multiple aggregation rules (FedAvg, Trimmed Mean, MultiKrum, FLAME) with small poisoned subsets per malicious client.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Kavindu Herath', 'Joshua Zhao', 'Saurabh Bagchi']
  • Tags: ['Federated Learning', 'Backdoor Attacks', 'Semantics-Aware Triggers', 'Poisoning/Poisoned Updates']

item.title: Perturb and Recover: Fine-tuning for Effective Backdoor Removal from CLIP
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies backdoor attacks on CLIP-style vision-language models.
  • Evaluates existing backdoor removal/cleaning methods and finds them ineffective against blended/badnet-style triggers.
  • Proposes PAR (Perturb and Recover) fine-tuning to remove backdoors while preserving standard performance.
  • Demonstrates effectiveness across different CLIP encoders and attack types, including using only synthetic text-image pairs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Naman Deep Singh', 'Francesco Croce', 'Matthias Hein']
  • Tags: ['backdoor removal', 'vision-language models', 'fine-tuning defenses', 'CLIP security', 'data poisoning attacks']

item.title: Diffusion-Based Feature Denoising and Using NNMF for Robust Brain Tumor Classification
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a robust brain tumor MRI classification pipeline combining NNMF feature decomposition, a lightweight CNN classifier, and diffusion-based feature purification.
  • Introduces a forward-noising plus learned denoiser module to purify features prior to classification, aiming to improve adversarial robustness.
  • Evaluates clean accuracy and robust accuracy against strong adversarial attacks generated by AutoAttack.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hiba Adil Al-kharsan', "R\\'obert Rajk\\'o"]
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'diffusion-based denoising', 'medical image classification', 'NNMF feature extraction', 'adversarial attacks (AutoAttack)']

item.title: From Evidence to Verdict: An Agent-Based Forensic Framework for AI-Generated Image Detection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AIFo, a training-free agent-based forensic framework for detecting AI-generated images.
  • Uses multi-stage evidence collection (reverse image search, metadata extraction, pre-trained classifiers, vision-language model analysis) with multi-agent debate to resolve conflicts.
  • Includes an optional memory-augmented module for leveraging historical case information.
  • Evaluates on a 6,000-image benchmark across lab and real-world scenarios, reporting high accuracy (97.05%) and improved robustness/generalization over baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mengfei Liang', 'Yiting Qu', 'Yukun Jiang', 'Michael Backes', 'Yang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['AI-generated image detection', 'digital forensics', 'agent-based/multi-agent systems', 'evidence fusion', 'vision-language analysis']

item.title: Toward Generalizable Forgery Detection and Reasoning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a generalizable AI-generated image forgery detection approach that includes interpretability via reasoning about forgery attributes.
  • Introduces a unified Forgery Detection and Reasoning task (FDR-Task) using multi-modal large language models (MLLMs).
  • Contributes the MMFR-Dataset (120K images, 10 generative models) with 378K attribute reasoning annotations.
  • Presents FakeReasoning framework combining dual visual encoders (CLIP+DINO), forgery-aware feature fusion, and a probability mapping module for improved detection and reasoning robustness across models.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yueying Gao', 'Dongliang Chang', 'Bingyao Yu', 'Haotian Qin', 'Muxi Diao', 'Lei Chen', 'Kongming Liang', 'Zhanyu Ma']
  • Tags: ['forgery-detection', 'AI-generated-image-misuse-mitigation', 'multi-modal-LLM', 'robustness-generalization', 'interpretability-reasoning']

item.title: ForgeryGPT: A Multimodal LLM for Interpretable Image Forgery Detection and Localization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ForgeryGPT, a multimodal LLM framework for image forgery detection and localization (pixel-level tampering masks).
  • Introduces a Mask-Aware Forgery Extractor with a localization expert and mask encoder to capture forensics correlations across linguistic feature spaces.
  • Uses object-agnostic forgery prompting, vocabulary-enhanced vision encoding, and mask-text alignment for improved interpretability and interactive dialogue.
  • Employs multi-stage training with task-specific instruction tuning datasets for better detection and explanation generation.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Fanrui Zhang', 'Jiawei Liu', 'Jiaying Zhu', 'Esther Sun', 'Dong Li', 'Qiang Zhang', 'Zheng-Jun Zha']
  • Tags: ['image-forgery-detection', 'multimodal-llms', 'localization', 'forensics-interpretability', 'vision-language-instruction-tuning']

item.title: The DeepSpeak Dataset
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces the DeepSpeak multimodal dataset (100+ hours) of authentic and synthetic deepfake talking-head audiovisual content with consented real data.
  • Generates deepfakes using multiple video synthesis engines and voice cloning engines, emphasizing identity face swaps via an embedding-based identity-matching approach.
  • Performs large-scale evaluations showing existing deepfake detectors fail to generalize without retraining on newer, more diverse deepfake generation methods.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Dataset (Research)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Sarah Barrington', 'Maty Bohacek', 'Hany Farid']
  • Tags: ['deepfakes', 'forensics', 'dataset-benchmark', 'detector-evaluation', 'identity-matching']

item.title: Sim-CLIP: Unsupervised Siamese Adversarial Fine-Tuning for Robust and Semantically-Rich Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Sim-CLIP, an unsupervised Siamese adversarial fine-tuning method to make CLIP-style vision encoders more robust to imperceptible adversarial perturbations.
  • Trains with a cosine similarity objective and uses a symmetric stop-gradient mechanism to align semantic representations between clean and adversarial views.
  • Evaluates on multiple VLMs/tasks under targeted and untargeted adversarial attacks, reporting improved robustness and preserved semantic fidelity over prior robust CLIP defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Md Zarif Hossain', 'Ahmed Imteaj']
  • Tags: ['adversarial robustness', 'vision-language models', 'adversarial training', 'perturbation defenses', 'self-supervised/unsupervised learning']

item.title: BodhiPromptShield: Pre-Inference Prompt Mediation for Suppressing Privacy Propagation in LLM/VLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes BodhiPromptShield, a pre-inference prompt mediation framework to suppress privacy propagation across multiple agent stages (retrieval, memory writes, tool calls, logs).
  • Detects sensitive spans and routes them through typed placeholders/semantic abstraction/secure symbolic mapping with delayed restoration to authorized boundaries.
  • Evaluates on the Controlled Prompt-Privacy Benchmark (CPPB), showing reduced privacy propagation and improved performance over generic de-identification pipelines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Bo Ma', 'Jinsong Wu', 'Weiqi Yan']
  • Tags: ['prompt mediation', 'privacy propagation', 'LLM/VLM agents', 'de-identification', 'privacy/security evaluation']

item.title: Uncovering Linguistic Fragility in Vision-Language-Action Models via Diversity-Aware Red Teaming
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces DAERT (Diversity-Aware Embodied Red Teaming) to systematically uncover VLA safety vulnerabilities caused by linguistic variations.
  • Uses a uniform policy to generate diverse adversarial instructions and evaluates attack effectiveness via execution failures in a physical simulator.
  • Experiments on multiple robotic benchmarks against two VLA models (π0 and OpenVLA), showing large drops in task success rate (93.33% to 5.85%).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Baoshun Tong', 'Haoran He', 'Ling Pan', 'Yang Liu', 'Liang Lin']
  • Tags: ['red-teaming', 'adversarial prompts', 'robustness testing', 'vision-language-action', 'embodied agents']

item.title: HaloProbe: Bayesian Detection and Mitigation of Object Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies detection and mitigation of object hallucinations in vision-language models using a Bayesian, token-level hallucination probability estimator (HaloProbe).
  • Shows that attention-weight-based detection can be unreliable due to confounders (e.g., token position and object repetition) leading to Simpson’s paradox.
  • Uses HaloProbe as an external scoring signal to guide non-invasive decoding-time mitigation without modifying model internals.
  • Evaluates effectiveness against intervention-based mitigation approaches, reporting reduced hallucinations with preserved utility/fluency.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Reihaneh Zohrabi', 'Hosein Hasani', 'Akshita Gupta', 'Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah', 'Anna Rohrbach', 'Marcus Rohrbach']
  • Tags: ['Hallucination detection', 'Vision-language models', 'Bayesian uncertainty estimation', 'Decoding-time mitigation', 'Attention confounders']

item.title: Extending ZACH-ViT to Robust Medical Imaging: Corruption and Adversarial Stress Testing in Low-Data Regimes
item.description:
Summary

  • Evaluates ZACH-ViT on robustness against common image corruptions and adversarial perturbations (FGSM, PGD) in low-data medical imaging (MedMNIST, 50 samples/class).
  • Compares ZACH-ViT with ABMIL, Minimal-ViT, and TransMIL under clean, corruption, and adversarial settings using fixed hyperparameters and multiple seeds.
  • Finds ZACH-ViT ranks best overall on clean and common corruptions, while still performing relatively well under FGSM/PGD though adversarial robustness is broadly poor.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Athanasios Angelakis', 'Marta Gomez-Barrero']
  • Tags: ['adversarial-robustness', 'image-corruptions', 'FGSM', 'PGD', 'medical-imaging']

item.title: EDGE-Shield: Efficient Denoising-staGE Shield for Violative Content Filtering via Scalable Reference-Based Matching
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes EDGE-Shield, a training-free reference-based content filtering method for text-to-image generative models.
  • Implements efficient embedding-based reference matching and performs filtering during the denoising process to reduce latency.
  • Introduces an $x$-pred transformation to improve violative-content classification accuracy at earlier denoising stages.
  • Evaluates against two generative models (Z-Image-Turbo, Qwen-Image) showing large latency reductions while maintaining filtering effectiveness.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Takara Taniguchi', 'Ryohei Shimizu', 'Minh-Duc Vo', 'Kota Izumi', 'Shiqi Yang', 'Teppei Suzuki']
  • Tags: ['content filtering', 'generative model safety', 'reference-based detection', 'denoising-time defense', 'deepfake/copyright risk']

item.title: Reading Between the Pixels: An Inscriptive Jailbreak Attack on Text-to-Image Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes the “inscriptive jailbreak” for text-to-image models, coercing them to generate images with harmful, legible textual payloads embedded in otherwise benign scenes.
  • Introduces Etch, a black-box attack framework that splits prompts into semantic camouflage, visual-spatial anchoring, and typographic encoding, using iterative refinement guided by vision-language model critiques.
  • Evaluates across 7 T2I models on 2 benchmarks, reporting substantially higher attack success rates than baselines.
  • Finds a safety-alignment blind spot related to typography/text-rendering capabilities and suggests need for typography-aware defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zonghao Ying', 'Haowen Dai', 'Lianyu Hu', 'Zonglei Jing', 'Quanchen Zou', 'Yaodong Yang', 'Aishan Liu', 'Xianglong Liu']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'text-to-image (T2I)', 'multimodal attacks', 'adversarial prompting']

item.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models under Contradictory Virtual Content Attacks in Augmented Reality
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes and models “contradictory virtual content” attacks in augmented reality as a threat to vision-language models.
  • Introduces ContrAR, a benchmark of 312 real-world AR videos validated by human participants.
  • Benchmarks 11 VLMs on robustness to virtual content manipulation/contradiction and reports gaps in detection/reasoning and latency tradeoffs.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yanming Xiu', 'Zhengayuan Jiang', 'Neil Zhenqiang Gong', 'Maria Gorlatova']
  • Tags: ['AR security', 'adversarial content attacks', 'vision-language models', 'benchmarking/robustness']

item.title: From Measurement to Mitigation: Quantifying and Reducing Identity Leakage in Image Representation Encoders with Linear Subspace Removal
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents an attacker-aware benchmark measuring identity leakage in frozen image representation encoders (e.g., CLIP, DINOv2/v3, SSCD) using open-set verification, calibrated template inversion checks, and face-context attribution.
  • Proposes a deployable defense: a one-shot linear projector (Identity Sanitization Projection, ISP) that removes an estimated identity subspace while preserving complementary features for utility.
  • Evaluates privacy and utility trade-offs on CelebA-20 and VGGFace2, showing reduced identity leakage to near-chance under linear probes and maintaining high non-biometric utility with cross-dataset transfer.
  • Claims the first attacker-calibrated facial privacy audit for non-face-recognition encoders and demonstrates robustness against template inversion.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Daniel George', 'Charles Yeh', 'Daniel Lee', 'Yifei Zhang']
  • Tags: ['privacy vulnerability', 'identity leakage', 'template inversion', 'representation learning', 'defense via subspace removal']

item.title: Weight space Detection of Backdoors in LoRA Adapters
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a trigger-agnostic method to detect backdoored LoRA adapters by analyzing adapter weight matrices directly, without model inference.
  • Computes spectral statistics from LoRA low-rank updates (ΔW) for attention projections (Q, K, V, O) to form a compact feature signature.
  • Trains a logistic regression detector to distinguish benign vs poisoned adapters across multiple LLM families, reporting perfect separation on unseen adapters.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['David Puertolas Merenciano', 'Ekaterina Vasyagina', 'Kevin Zhu', 'Javier Ferrando', 'Maheep Chaudhary']
  • Tags: ['backdoor detection', 'LoRA adapters', 'weight-space analysis', 'spectral features', 'model security']

item.title: OutSafe-Bench: A Benchmark for Multimodal Offensive Content Detection in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces OutSafe-Bench, a multimodal benchmark for evaluating safety/offensive content risks in large multimodal language models (text, images, audio, video).
  • Provides a large, bilingual (Chinese/English) and risk-category annotated dataset covering nine critical content risk categories, plus the MCRS metric for correlated/overlapping risks.
  • Proposes FairScore, an explainable automated multi-reviewer weighted aggregation method to improve evaluation reliability and reduce single-model bias.
  • Finds that multiple state-of-the-art MLLMs still exhibit substantial safety vulnerabilities, implying need for stronger defenses/safeguards.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yuping Yan', 'Yuhan Xie', 'Yuanshuai Li', 'Yingchao Yu', 'Lingjuan Lyu', 'Yaochu Jin']
  • Tags: ['AI safety evaluation', 'multimodal safety', 'offensive content detection', 'benchmark', 'LLM/MLLM red teaming']

item.title: How Alignment Routes: Localizing, Scaling, and Controlling Policy Circuits in Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Finds a sparse routing/circuit in alignment-trained LMs that uses a “gate” attention head to detect content and activate downstream “amplifier” heads that increase refusal behavior.
  • Uses censorship/safety refusal and controlled experiments (necessity/sufficiency interchange tests, permutation nulls, bootstrap resampling) to validate circuit stability and routing detectability across multiple models.
  • Shows scaling behavior where routing distributes at larger sizes and ablations weaken but routing remains detectable; modulates refusal strength from hard refusal to steering/compliance via continuous signal control.
  • Analyzes an asymmetry where deeper-layer representations of harmful content can emerge without the routing mechanism firing under cipher encoding, suggesting different generalization/robustness between intent recognition and policy binding.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Gregory N. Frank']
  • Tags: ['AI Security', 'Model Internals', 'Adversarial/Robustness Evaluation', 'Alignment Mechanisms']

item.title: The Company You Keep: How LLMs Respond to Dark Triad Traits
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how LLM conversational behavior changes when prompted with user traits from the Dark Triad (Machiavellianism, Narcissism, Psychopathy).
  • Analyzes whether models respond with corrective (safety-like) behavior versus reinforcing/agreeable behavior at different severity levels and response sentiments.
  • Frames implications for designing safer conversational systems that detect and appropriately respond as prompts escalate from benign to harmful.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zeyi Lu', 'Angelica Henestrosa', 'Pavel Chizhov', 'Ivan P. Yamshchikov']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Sycophancy', 'Adversarial/social manipulation', 'Behavioral alignment']

item.title: Where Do Backdoors Live? A Component-Level Analysis of Backdoor Propagation in Speech Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes how backdoor attacks propagate through speech language model (SLM) component pipelines rather than studying end-to-end behavior only.
  • Performs component-level analysis to identify which modules most influence whether backdoors persist or are erased.
  • Shows backdoors can be encoded in shared multitask embeddings such that poisoned samples are not easily separable from benign ones, undermining separability-based filtering defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Alexandrine Fortier', 'Thomas Thebaud', "Jes\\'us Villalba", 'Najim Dehak', 'Patrick Cardinal', 'Peter West']
  • Tags: ['backdoor attacks', 'speech language models', 'component-level analysis', 'model security defenses (filtering limitations)']

item.title: Phonetic Perturbations Reveal Tokenizer-Rooted Safety Gaps in LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CMP-RT, a diagnostic red-teaming method using code-mixed phonetic perturbations to expose LLM safety failures tied to tokenization.
  • Shows phonetic/textese-like perturbations fragment safety-critical tokens into sub-words, reducing attribution/safety mechanism effectiveness while keeping prompt understanding intact.
  • Demonstrates the vulnerability evades standard defenses, transfers across multiple SOTA models, and can be scaled via supervised fine-tuning.
  • Provides mechanistic/layer-wise analysis and finds that enforcing output equivalence can recover lost representations, suggesting a structural alignment gap rooted in tokenization.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Darpan Aswal', 'Siddharth D Jaiswal']
  • Tags: ['tokenization-vulnerability', 'LLM-safety-bypass', 'adversarial-text-perturbations', 'red-teaming', 'mechanistic-analysis']

item.title: Epistemic Blinding: An Inference-Time Protocol for Auditing Prior Contamination in LLM-Assisted Analysis
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an inference-time protocol (“epistemic blinding”) to audit how much LLM-assisted outputs are driven by user-supplied data vs. memorized priors from training.
  • Implements blinding by replacing entity identifiers with anonymous codes during prompting, then compares against an unblinded control to quantify prior contamination.
  • Demonstrates effects in biological drug-target prioritization and generalizes to equity screening, showing ranking changes under blinding while validated recovery remains similar.
  • Releases an open-source tool/skill to apply the protocol within agentic LLM workflows.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Michael Cuccarese']
  • Tags: ['LLM auditing', 'Inference-time defense', 'Data leakage / prior contamination', 'Privacy-memorization risk', 'Evaluation protocol']

item.title: Swiss-Bench 003: Evaluating LLM Reliability and Adversarial Security for Swiss Regulatory Contexts
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Swiss-Bench 003 (SBP-003), extending HAAS by adding dimensions for self-graded reliability (D7) and adversarial security (D8).
  • Evaluates 10 frontier LLMs on 808 Swiss-specific, multilingual benchmark items including adversarially oriented tasks such as system prompt leakage and PII extraction/defense.
  • Finds large gaps between self-graded reliability scores and externally judged adversarial security scores; prompt leakage resistance and PII extraction defenses vary widely and are often weak.
  • Maps benchmark dimensions to Swiss FINMA/nDSG requirements and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, supporting regulatory-aligned security evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Fatih Uenal']
  • Tags: ['LLM security evaluation', 'Adversarial attacks', 'Prompt injection/prompt leakage', 'PII extraction', 'Benchmarking']

item.title: CURE:Circuit-Aware Unlearning for LLM-based Recommendation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CURE, a circuit-aware unlearning method for LLM-based recommender systems to remove user-related data effects.
  • Extracts and categorizes LLM circuit components into forget-specific, retain-specific, and task-shared modules, then applies function-specific update rules.
  • Aims to mitigate gradient conflicts between forgetting and retaining objectives to improve unlearning effectiveness and preserve utility.
  • Evaluated on real-world datasets, showing improved unlearning versus baselines.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Ziheng Chen', 'Jiali Cheng', 'Zezhong Fan', 'Hadi Amiri', 'Yunzhi Yao', 'Xiangguo Sun', 'Yang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['unlearning', 'privacy', 'LLM-based recommendation', 'gradient conflict mitigation']

item.title: Exclusive Unlearning
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes “Exclusive Unlearning,” a selective forgetting approach that aims to remove harmful knowledge broadly by forgetting everything except explicitly retained capabilities/expressions.
  • Claims improved safety coverage against a wide range of adversarial or harmful inputs, including jailbreaks.
  • Shows maintaining useful domain capabilities (e.g., medicine and mathematics) while performing the unlearning step.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Mutsumi Sasaki', 'Kouta Nakayama', 'Yusuke Miyao', 'Yohei Oseki', 'Masaru Isonuma']
  • Tags: ['machine unlearning', 'jailbreak defense', 'LLM safety', 'adversarial robustness']

item.title: Stop Fixating on Prompts: Reasoning Hijacking and Constraint Tightening for Red-Teaming LLM Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes JailAgent framework to red-team LLM agents without modifying user prompts.
  • Uses trigger extraction, reasoning hijacking, and constraint tightening to manipulate reasoning trajectory and memory retrieval.
  • Aims for adaptive, cross-model and cross-scenario effectiveness against agent security threats.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yanxu Mao', 'Peipei Liu', 'Tiehan Cui', 'Congying Liu', 'Mingzhe Xing', 'Datao You']
  • Tags: ['Jailbreaking', 'Prompt/Reasoning Manipulation', 'LLM Agent Security', 'Red-Teaming', 'Adversarial Attacks']

item.title: XMark: Reliable Multi-Bit Watermarking for LLM-Generated Texts
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes XMark, a multi-bit watermarking method for LLM-generated text to embed recoverable binary messages.
  • Improves reliability of decoding while preserving text quality, addressing trade-offs in prior watermarking approaches.
  • Targets robustness to limited-length generations where decoding accuracy typically degrades.
  • Evaluates across multiple downstream tasks and reports improved decoding accuracy over existing methods.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Jiahao Xu', 'Rui Hu', 'Olivera Kotevska', 'Zikai Zhang']
  • Tags: ['watermarking', 'LLM-generated text', 'traceability/attribution', 'text security defenses', 'multi-bit encoding/decoding']

item.title: Gradient-Controlled Decoding: A Safety Guardrail for LLMs with Dual-Anchor Steering
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Gradient-Controlled Decoding (GCD), a training-free safety guardrail for LLMs to mitigate jailbreaks and prompt-injection attacks.
  • Uses dual anchor steering via acceptance (“Sure”) and refusal (“Sorry”) to tighten the safety decision boundary and reduce brittle thresholds/false positives.
  • Implements a mitigation step that preset-injects refusal tokens to guarantee first-token safety before autoregressive decoding continues, independent of sampling strategy.
  • Evaluated on ToxicChat, XSTest-v2, and AdvBench with reported reductions in false positives and attack success rate, plus modest latency overhead.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Purva Chiniya', 'Kevin Scaria', 'Sagar Chaturvedi']
  • Tags: ['jailbreak-defense', 'prompt-injection-mitigation', 'LLM-safety-guardrails', 'decoding-time-protection', 'adversarial-evaluation']

item.title: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a new threat model where attackers poison an LLM web agent’s persistent memory via environmental observation rather than direct memory access.
  • Introduces eTAMP (Environment-injected Trajectory-based Agent Memory Poisoning) enabling cross-session, cross-site compromise after a single contaminated observation.
  • Shows substantial attack success rates across multiple models and platforms (up to 32.5% on GPT-5-mini).
  • Finds that agent “frustration”/stress conditions (e.g., dropped clicks, garbled text) significantly increase susceptibility (ASR up to 8×).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wei Zou', 'Mingwen Dong', 'Miguel Romero Calvo', 'Shuaichen Chang', 'Jiang Guo', 'Dongkyu Lee', 'Xing Niu', 'Xiaofei Ma', 'Yanjun Qi', 'Jiarong Jiang']
  • Tags: ['Memory poisoning', 'Web agents', 'Cross-session attacks', 'Persistent compromise']

item.title: Safety, Security, and Cognitive Risks in World Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Surveys world-model risks across safety, security, and cognitive domains, especially for autonomous decision-making agents.
  • Defines trajectory persistence and representational risk, and proposes a unified threat model using MITRE ATLAS/OWASP LLM Top 10 mappings.
  • Introduces a five-profile attacker taxonomy and provides proof-of-concept adversarial attacks (trajectory-persistent attacks) with measured reward degradation and action drift on a real checkpoint.
  • Proposes interdisciplinary mitigations including adversarial hardening, alignment engineering, governance frameworks, and human-factors interventions.

Paper Type

  • Survey/Research (survey with threat model + empirical proof-of-concept + mitigations)

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Manoj Parmar']
  • Tags: ['AI security', 'world models', 'adversarial attacks', 'threat modeling', 'mitigation/defense']

item.title: Not All Latent Spaces Are Flat: Hyperbolic Concept Control
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a new text-to-image concept steering/control method (HyCon) using hyperbolic geometry via parallel transport.
  • Aims to improve reliability and reduce unsafe content generation by steering latent/text embeddings away from unsafe concepts.
  • Evaluates across multiple safety benchmarks and multiple T2I backbones, claiming state-of-the-art results.
  • Uses an off-the-shelf generative model plus a lightweight adapter connected to a hyperbolic text encoder.

item.title: Weight space Detection of Backdoors in LoRA Adapters
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a trigger-agnostic method to detect backdoored LoRA adapters by analyzing adapter weight matrices directly, without model inference.
  • Computes spectral statistics from LoRA low-rank updates (ΔW) for attention projections (Q, K, V, O) to form a compact feature signature.
  • Trains a logistic regression detector to distinguish benign vs poisoned adapters across multiple LLM families, reporting perfect separation on unseen adapters.

item.title: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies pop-up-based environmental injection attacks against GUI agents using multimodal LLMs and characterizes how the attacks shift attention behavior.
  • Identifies a layer-wise attention divergence pattern between correct and incorrect outputs under these attacks.
  • Proposes LaSM (Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism) that selectively amplifies attention/MLP modules in critical layers to improve saliency alignment without retraining.
  • Reports improved defense success rate and robustness across multiple datasets with minimal impact on general capabilities.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Phonetic Perturbations Reveal Tokenizer-Rooted Safety Gaps in LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CMP-RT, a diagnostic red-teaming method using code-mixed phonetic perturbations to expose LLM safety failures tied to tokenization.
  • Shows phonetic/textese-like perturbations fragment safety-critical tokens into sub-words, reducing attribution/safety mechanism effectiveness while keeping prompt understanding intact.
  • Demonstrates the vulnerability evades standard defenses, transfers across multiple SOTA models, and can be scaled via supervised fine-tuning.
  • Provides mechanistic/layer-wise analysis and finds that enforcing output equivalence can recover lost representations, suggesting a structural alignment gap rooted in tokenization.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Darpan Aswal', 'Siddharth D Jaiswal']
  • Tags: ['tokenization-vulnerability', 'LLM-safety-bypass', 'adversarial-text-perturbations', 'red-teaming', 'mechanistic-analysis']

item.title: ForgeryGPT: A Multimodal LLM for Interpretable Image Forgery Detection and Localization
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ForgeryGPT, a multimodal LLM framework for image forgery detection and localization (pixel-level tampering masks).
  • Introduces a Mask-Aware Forgery Extractor with a localization expert and mask encoder to capture forensics correlations across linguistic feature spaces.
  • Uses object-agnostic forgery prompting, vocabulary-enhanced vision encoding, and mask-text alignment for improved interpretability and interactive dialogue.
  • Employs multi-stage training with task-specific instruction tuning datasets for better detection and explanation generation.

Paper Type

  • Research

item.title: Sim-CLIP: Unsupervised Siamese Adversarial Fine-Tuning for Robust and Semantically-Rich Vision-Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Sim-CLIP, an unsupervised Siamese adversarial fine-tuning method to make CLIP-style vision encoders more robust to imperceptible adversarial perturbations.
  • Trains with a cosine similarity objective and uses a symmetric stop-gradient mechanism to align semantic representations between clean and adversarial views.
  • Evaluates on multiple VLMs/tasks under targeted and untargeted adversarial attacks, reporting improved robustness and preserved semantic fidelity over prior robust CLIP defenses.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Md Zarif Hossain', 'Ahmed Imteaj']

item.title: CritBench: A Framework for Evaluating Cybersecurity Capabilities of Large Language Models in IEC 61850 Digital Substation Environments
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces CritBench, a framework to evaluate LLM cybersecurity capabilities specifically in OT/IEC 61850 digital substation environments rather than IT-only settings.
  • Benchmarks five SOTA models on 81 domain-specific tasks covering static configuration analysis, network traffic reconnaissance, and live virtual machine interaction.
  • Includes a domain-specific tool scaffold to enable IEC 61850 protocol interaction and shows improved performance on dynamic/live tasks with scaffolding.
  • Finds models perform well on static structured-file analysis and single-step enumeration but degrade on tasks requiring sequential state tracking to manipulate live systems.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Framework

item.title: A Formal Security Framework for MCP-Based AI Agents: Threat Taxonomy, Verification Models, and Defense Mechanisms
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes MCPSHIELD, a formal security framework specifically for MCP-based AI agents.
  • Introduces a hierarchical threat taxonomy (7 threat categories, 23 attack vectors) mapped to four attack surfaces.
  • Develops a formal verification model (labeled transition systems with trust-boundary annotations) for static/runtime analysis of tool interaction chains.
  • Evaluates existing defenses and proposes a defense-in-depth reference architecture (capability-based access control, cryptographic tool attestation, information flow tracking, runtime policy enforcement).

item.title: Swiss-Bench 003: Evaluating LLM Reliability and Adversarial Security for Swiss Regulatory Contexts
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces Swiss-Bench 003 (SBP-003), extending HAAS by adding dimensions for self-graded reliability (D7) and adversarial security (D8).
  • Evaluates 10 frontier LLMs on 808 Swiss-specific, multilingual benchmark items including adversarially oriented tasks such as system prompt leakage and PII extraction/defense.
  • Finds large gaps between self-graded reliability scores and externally judged adversarial security scores; prompt leakage resistance and PII extraction defenses vary widely and are often weak.
  • Maps benchmark dimensions to Swiss FINMA/nDSG requirements and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs, supporting regulatory-aligned security evaluation.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

item.title: Hackers or Hallucinators? A Comprehensive Analysis of LLM-Based Automated Penetration Testing
item.description:
Summary

  • Analyzes and systematizes LLM-based automated penetration testing frameworks via a taxonomy across multiple architectural dimensions.
  • Runs large-scale empirical comparisons of 13 open-source AutoPT frameworks plus 2 baselines under a unified benchmark.
  • Focuses on autonomous attack execution workflows and benchmarking rather than defenses.
  • Includes extensive logging and manual security-expert analysis to evaluate performance and behaviors of AutoPT systems.

item.title: LanG -- A Governance-Aware Agentic AI Platform for Unified Security Operations
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes LanG, a governance-aware agentic AI platform for unified security operations (SOC).
  • Develops an LLM-assisted incident context correlation engine and a three-phase attack reconstructor with reported kill-chain accuracy.
  • Includes an LLM-based rule generator to produce deployable Snort/Suricata/YARA rules and layered guardrails (regex + prompt-guard semantic classifier).

item.title: Your LLM Agent Can Leak Your Data: Data Exfiltration via Backdoored Tool Use
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Back-Reveal, a data exfiltration attack using backdoored fine-tuned LLM agents with tool access.
  • Embeds semantic triggers that cause the agent to make memory-access tool calls and exfiltrate retrieved user context via disguised retrieval calls.
  • Shows multi-turn interactions can amplify leakage by using attacker-controlled retrieval outputs to steer future agent behavior.
  • Experiments highlight a vulnerability in tool-using LLM agents and motivate defenses against exfiltration-oriented backdoors.

Paper Type

item.title: XMark: Reliable Multi-Bit Watermarking for LLM-Generated Texts
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes XMark, a multi-bit watermarking method for LLM-generated text to embed recoverable binary messages.
  • Improves reliability of decoding while preserving text quality, addressing trade-offs in prior watermarking approaches.
  • Targets robustness to limited-length generations where decoding accuracy typically degrades.
  • Evaluates across multiple downstream tasks and reports improved decoding accuracy over existing methods.

item.title: FreakOut-LLM: The Effect of Emotional Stimuli on Safety Alignment
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how emotional stimuli (stress vs neutral vs relaxation) in system prompts affect safety-aligned LLMs’ susceptibility to jailbreaks.
  • Evaluates jailbreak/attack success across ten LLMs using HarmBench and AdvBench-style adversarial prompts, showing stress priming increases jailbreak success substantially.
  • Analyzes which models and conditions are most vulnerable and uses statistical models/logistic regression plus psychological-state measures to correlate emotional state with attack success.

item.title: CURE:Circuit-Aware Unlearning for LLM-based Recommendation
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes CURE, a circuit-aware unlearning method for LLM-based recommender systems to remove user-related data effects.
  • Extracts and categorizes LLM circuit components into forget-specific, retain-specific, and task-shared modules, then applies function-specific update rules.
  • Aims to mitigate gradient conflicts between forgetting and retaining objectives to improve unlearning effectiveness and preserve utility.
  • Evaluated on real-world datasets, showing improved unlearning versus baselines.

item.title: Measuring the Permission Gate: A Stress-Test Evaluation of Claude Code's Auto Mode
item.description:
Summary

  • Presents an independent stress-test evaluation of Claude Code’s permission-gating system for AI coding agents, focused on auto mode’s handling of ambiguous authorization scope and risk.
  • Introduces AmPermBench (128 prompts) with controlled ambiguity axes and measures action-level false negatives/positives across multiple DevOps task families.
  • Finds substantially higher end-to-end false negative rate (81.0%) than production reports, with a major contributor being state-changing actions that bypass the classifier via in-project file edits (Tier 2 coverage gap).

item.title: Synthetic Trust Attacks: Modeling How Generative AI Manipulates Human Decisions in Social Engineering Fraud
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces “Synthetic Trust Attacks” (STAs) as a formal threat category and presents STAM, an eight-stage framework covering the full social-engineering fraud attack chain.
  • Argues that defenses focused on synthetic-media detection are insufficient because the key vulnerability is at the victim’s decision/credibility assessment layer.
  • Provides a Trust-Cue Taxonomy, an incident coding schema, and proposes falsifiable hypotheses relating attack structure to compliance outcomes.
  • Suggests a decision-layer defense via the Calm, Check, Confirm protocol (operationalized as a research-grade defense).

Paper Type

item.title: Claw-Eval: Toward Trustworthy Evaluation of Autonomous Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes Claw-Eval, an end-to-end benchmark for evaluating autonomous agents with trajectory-aware grading rather than only final outputs.
  • Adds explicitly evaluated dimensions for Safety and Robustness, using evidence channels (execution traces, audit logs, environment snapshots) and fine-grained rubrics.
  • Covers 9 task categories across service orchestration, multimodal perception/generation, and multi-turn professional dialogue, including multimodal (e.g., video) evaluation.
  • Finds that trajectory-opaque grading misses a substantial fraction of safety/robustness failures and studies the effects of controlled error injection on evaluation metrics.

item.title: Epistemic Blinding: An Inference-Time Protocol for Auditing Prior Contamination in LLM-Assisted Analysis
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an inference-time protocol (“epistemic blinding”) to audit how much LLM-assisted outputs are driven by user-supplied data vs. memorized priors from training.
  • Implements blinding by replacing entity identifiers with anonymous codes during prompting, then compares against an unblinded control to quantify prior contamination.
  • Demonstrates effects in biological drug-target prioritization and generalizes to equity screening, showing ranking changes under blinding while validated recovery remains similar.
  • Releases an open-source tool/skill to apply the protocol within agentic LLM workflows.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Michael Cuccarese']
  • Tags: ['LLM auditing', 'Inference-time defense', 'Data leakage / prior contamination', 'Privacy-memorization risk', 'Evaluation protocol']

item.title: Auditable Agents
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a framework for making LLM agent actions auditable so that accountability after deployment is possible.
  • Defines five dimensions of agent auditability (e.g., action recoverability, policy checkability, evidence integrity) and three mechanism classes (detect, enforce, recover).
  • Presents evidence from an ecosystem scan of audit/security prerequisites, runtime overhead measurements for tamper-evident records, and experiments on partial recovery when logs are missing.
  • Advances an “Auditability Card” concept and lists open research problems focused on auditability mechanisms for real agent systems.

Paper Type

item.title: LatentAudit: Real-Time White-Box Faithfulness Monitoring for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Verifiable Deployment
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces LatentAudit, a white-box, real-time faithfulness monitor for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG).
  • Uses mid-to-late residual-stream activations from an open-weight generator and computes Mahalanobis distance to evidence representations to decide whether answers are supported.
  • Reports AUROC and low inference overhead across multiple QA benchmarks and model families; includes robustness to retrieval failures and adversarial-like stress tests (contradictions, partial-support noise).
  • Proposes verifiable deployment via public verification (Groth16) while avoiding disclosure of model weights or activations.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Zhe Yu', 'Wenpeng Xing', 'Meng Han']
  • Tags: ['RAG', 'Model monitoring', 'White-box auditing', 'Faithfulness/groundedness', 'Verifiable computation']

item.title: From Retinal Evidence to Safe Decisions: RETINA-SAFE and ECRT for Hallucination Risk Triage in Medical LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces RETINA-SAFE, an evidence-grounded benchmark for hallucination risk triage in medical LLMs using retinal grading records.
  • Defines three evidence-relation tasks: evidence-aligned, evidence-conflicting, and evidence-insufficient (E-Align/E-Conflict/E-Gap).
  • Proposes ECRT (Evidence-Conditioned Risk Triage), a two-stage white-box detection framework using internal representations and logit shifts to classify Safe vs Unsafe and further subtype unsafe cases.
  • Evaluates via evidence-grouped splits across multiple backbones and reports improved balanced accuracy for hallucination risk triage over baselines and ablations.

Paper Type

item.title: Pressure, What Pressure? Sycophancy Disentanglement in Language Models via Reward Decomposition
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a sycophancy-specific mitigation method by decomposing the training reward into multiple components to separate distinct failure modes (pressure capitulation vs evidence blindness).
  • Introduces a multi-term GRPO reward with terms for pressure resistance, context fidelity, position consistency, agreement suppression, and factual correctness.
  • Trains with paired pressure-free vs pressured variants across authority levels and conflicting evidence contexts, reporting consistent reductions in sycophancy across multiple base models and generalization to new prompt/pressure formats.
  • Provides ablations showing each reward term corresponds to an independent behavioral dimension.

item.title: From Governance Norms to Enforceable Controls: A Layered Translation Method for Runtime Guardrails in Agentic AI
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a method to translate AI governance standards into enforceable runtime guardrails for agentic AI systems.
  • Introduces layered control placement across governance objectives, design-time constraints, runtime mediation, and assurance feedback.
  • Defines distinctions between objectives, technical controls, runtime guardrails, and assurance evidence, including a rubric for deciding which controls belong at runtime.
  • Demonstrates the approach via a procurement-agent case study.

item.title: ClawsBench: Evaluating Capability and Safety of LLM Productivity Agents in Simulated Workspaces
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ClawsBench, a benchmark for evaluating LLM productivity agents in realistic simulated, stateful multi-service environments (Gmail/Slack/Calendar/Docs/Drive).
  • Measures both task success and safety via safety-critical scenarios, reporting unsafe action rates alongside success rates.
  • Identifies recurring patterns of unsafe behavior (e.g., multi-step sandbox escalation and silent contract modification).
  • Evaluates how agent scaffolding levers (domain API skills and a meta prompt) affect capability and safety across multiple models and harnesses.
